Article Title: Amit Shah visits injured after deadly stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja pandal
Article Text:
Kolkata stampede kills 19, Amit Shah visits injured at hospital

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday visited Calcutta Medical College and Hospital, where people injured in the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata are undergoing treatment.At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in the stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening, following a surge in the crowd amid rain.Kolkata Police have registered a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the incident, an officer said. Police are also working to identify those killed in the stampede.Shah had earlier expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, describing the incident as “extremely distressing”. He also said he had spoken to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari to take stock of the situation.Following the tragedy, Kolkata Police imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, in parts of the city for three days, from October 18 to October 20, to maintain law and order.According to an order issued by Kolkata Police Commissioner Ajay Nand, the restrictions cover areas under the jurisdiction of Bowbazar police station, bounded by College Street, Central Avenue (CR Avenue), Colootola Street and Eden Hospital Road.The order prohibits unlawful assemblies of five or more people, carrying lathis or other lethal and dangerous weapons, and any activity likely to disturb public tranquillity or cause a breach of peace in the designated area.The order states: "Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by Sub-Section (1) of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 read with the Sub-Section (3) of the said Section, I, Ajay Nand, Commissioner of Police, Kolkata being an Executive Magistrate for the Metropolitan area of Kolkata as well as in the district of South 24 Parganas(within the limits of the suburbs of Kolkata falling under Kolkata police jurisdiction) do hereby prohibit for a period of 03(three) days from 18.10.2026 to 20.10.2026 or until further order, any unlawful assembly of 05(five) or more persons, carrying of lathi, any lethal or other dangerous weapons or doing of any act which is likely to cause breach of the peace and disturbances of the public tranquility within the said Area in the town of Kolkata. "The restrictions were imposed amid concerns that demonstrations, rallies and meetings could lead to violence and affect public safety. They will remain in force until October 20 or until further orders.
Article Summary: At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in the stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening. Kolkata Police have registered a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the incident.

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah Thursday said not just Left-wing extremism but every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.Addressing the event via video conferencing, Shah said the programme, organised under 'seva sankalp abhiyan' to mark 25 years of PM Modi's 'seva and samarpan' (service), would help tribal people who had lost limbs or sensory abilities due to Naxal violence. Chhattisgarh govt organised it with welfare organisations such as Bhagwan Mahaveer Viklang Sahayata Samiti and Bharatiya Jain Sanghatana to provide prosthetic devices, wheelchairs, crutches and hearing aids.Held in Jagdalpur from Oct 5 to 7, the campaign benefited over 3,600 persons with disabilities, including over 1,570 from Bastar. Shah said Maoists' use of IEDs to maim innocent civilians for political objectives was a grave human rights violation.Though violent Naxalism was eliminated by the March 31, 2026 deadline, Shah said, the task would remain unfinished until govt healed victims' wounds, helped them stand and ensured they lived with dignity.Bastar was becoming vibrant again, he said, citing participation in Bastar Olympics and Bastar Pandum. Shah said 8,526 Naxalites had surrendered. Accounts had been opened for 7,328, reward money given to 1,620, incentives provided to 7,882, jobs offered to 455 and land allotted to 129. Another 4,014 beneficiaries had received houses under PM Awas Yojana, while over 2,308 tribal people had undergone skill training.A total of 6,763 ration cards had been issued, 2,808 families provided free electricity and work begun on 372 road projects. 48,526 people had received Aadhaar cards and 44 gram panchayats were recognised under 'Ilwad Panchayat Awards'.Twenty of the 50 security camps in Chhattisgarh will be converted into Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera, providing public services, skill training and PDS benefits to nearby villages, Shah said. "The places where our security forces once sat to protect you will become the places where officials will lay the foundation for a developed Bastar," Shah added. tnn
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah said every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday claimed police personnel were keeping him under surveillance and said he could be detained overnight or on Friday morning, ahead of the outfit’s planned national flag-waving protest at Connaught Place.Addressing a press conference late Thursday, Dipke said he was prepared to go to jail for waving the Tricolour as the CJP called on supporters to gather at Central Park on Friday, despite the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) announcing a two-day closure of the venue.“Tomorrow, we will peacefully go and wave the Tiranga. The outfit has demanded Kumar’s resignation, alleging that more than 13 crore voters were deleted.Delhi Police has urged people to stay away from the gathering, citing prohibitory orders and saying Connaught Place is not a designated protest site. Article Title: A 7am email to employer, ‘I love you’ on clothes and a chilling ‘leaving this world’ note on wife’s birthday: What preceded Malayali techie couple’s deaths in Gurgaon flat
Article Text:
An IT professional, Mohammad Aslam, and his wife, Farhana, were discovered dead in their Gurgaon apartment.

Moved to Gurgaon three months ago

Email prompted colleagues to contact landlord





GURGAON: An email sent to his employer at around 7am, saying “we are leaving this world”, set off a chain of events that led to the discovery of an IT professional and his wife dead in their Gurgaon apartment on Wednesday.The techie had also shared the phone numbers of his parents and landlord, asking the company to inform them.When the landlord reached the flat in Tower 7 of M3M Marina, he found Mohammad Aslam (30) hanging and his wife, Farhana, who was about to turn 28, lying on the floor with an injury mark on her neck. He alerted Badshapur police station.Inside the flat, police found a note bearing the words “We are leaving this world”. The words “I love you” had also been scribbled on Farhana's clothes. Investigators are examining the messages and other material recovered from the apartment as they piece together what led to the couple’s deaths.Police suspect Aslam killed Farhana before dying by suicide, but said the sequence of events and the cause of death had not yet been established. A murder case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The couple’s families, based in Kerala, have been left struggling to understand what happened. Relatives said they knew of no marital discord and described the couple as being close to each other. They said Aslam had been undergoing treatment for depression for around a year and a half.“The couple shared a really close bond. Both were happy with each other and had no marital discord. There was no issue with the family either. But hearing this has left both families in shock,” said Faisal, Farhana’s brother.The couple had relocated to Gurgaon from Bengaluru around three months ago. Aslam, a native of Kozhikode, had joined an Indonesia-based IT company with an office in Sector 58. Farhana, who hailed from Malappuram, worked from home for an IT firm based in Bengaluru.They married in 2023 and spent around two years in Bengaluru before moving to Gurgaon.Aslam graduated in electrical and electronics engineering from NIT Calicut in 2018 and completed his MBA from IIM Indore in 2020. Farhana had completed her BTech from MES College of Engineering in Kuttippuram, Kerala.Family members said Aslam had been taking medication and undergoing therapy for depression for around 18 months. They said neither he nor Farhana had discussed any problems that might have suggested they were going through a difficult period.Faisal said relatives suspected work pressure could have contributed to the tragedy, although they had no confirmation of what the couple had been experiencing.“We used to go on trips together, and I connected very well with my brother-in-law. We suspect that work pressure in the IT sector may have led to the incident. They never discussed anything that suggested they were suffering or going through something so bad. Work pressure is the only reason we suspect, but only God and the two of them knew what was happening,” he said.Another relative, Abdul Azeez, said the family believed the incident may have occurred around midnight on Wednesday. Farhana was due to celebrate her birthday that day.“Her parents have been left shattered. We just want to take their bodies home,” he said.After Aslam’s email arrived around 7am on Wednesday, his colleagues contacted the landlord using the details provided. The landlord went to the apartment, found the couple dead and alerted the police.An emergency response vehicle reached the spot around 8am, followed by a larger police team. An officer said the flat’s door was not bolted.Police recovered three laptops, two mobile phones, a rope, the note, a diary, scissors and a pen drive from the apartment. The electronic devices were seized for forensic analysis. Police said the note contained no allegations against anyone.Both bodies were shifted to a mortuary and identified by family members on Friday. Autopsies were yet to be conducted.“The cause of death will be established only after the autopsy report. It is suspected that the husband killed his wife and later died by suicide after sending an email to his office,” the officer said.Police are examining the evidence to establish the circumstances and sequence of the deaths.
Article Summary: Mohammad Aslam, 30, and his wife, Farhana, 28, were found dead in their Gurgaon apartment. Police suspect Aslam killed his wife before committing suicide. Aslam sent an email to his employer at around 7am, saying “we are leaving this world’

NEW DELHI: An Emirates flight from Delhi to Dubai has been delayed by more than 14 hours after the aircraft reportedly suffered a bird strike while arriving in Delhi from Dubai on Saturday, October 17, the airline said in a statement.According to PTI, Flight EK 517, scheduled to depart from Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport at 4:25 pm on Saturday, is now expected to leave at 7 am on Sunday, October 18, local time, Emirates said.The airline said the aircraft would undergo necessary repairs following the incident. The backlash comes as the state government faces scrutiny over recent killings linked to the state's drug menace, with the Union home ministry seeking reports on the cases.BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh alleged that Mann's foreign trip, which he said coincided with the chief minister's birthday, was inappropriate at a time when Punjab was facing multiple crises.BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh alleged that Mann's foreign trip, which he said coincided with the chief minister's birthday, was inappropriate at a time when Punjab was facing multiple crises.""Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed... 23 police stations have been targeted in grenade attacks, and even police personnel feel unsafe while in uniform. At a time when all of Punjab is engulfed in a raging crisis, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has chosen to travel to France with his wife to celebrate his birthday. This is a deeply distressing situation," Chugh said on Saturday.Questioning the nature of the visit, the BJP leader alleged, "If this is an official state visit, how is his wife accompanying him? In reality, a birthday party is being hosted in France under the guise of an official state visit."Chugh also targeted the AAP government over the drug menace and security concerns, claiming that people opposing drug abuse were being killed and citing grenade attacks on police stations. "Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed," he said, alleging that even police personnel felt unsafe.The chief minister also faced criticism from Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia, who alleged that Mann had attended a police meeting in Phillaur on October 16 while under the influence of alcohol. I even tweeted today about 'An Evening in Paris', which is a famous Hindi song, 'Rang-rangiliyan manane gaye hain'."Majithia questioned the chief minister's handling of the drug issue, alleging that Mann had attended a meeting on the menace while intoxicated."Holding a meeting against drugs while being drunk as the Chief Minister, what on earth is happening?" he said.Separately, Congress leader Sachin Pilot criticised the Punjab government's handling of law and order, alleging that killings, extortion, ransom demands and encounters had become common in the state.Speaking during a visit to Moga district on Saturday, Pilot called for accountability and faster legal action in murder cases. He also referred to a family that, he alleged, had been waiting for justice and assistance three years after the death of a young man's father.The opposition attacks come amid continuing criticism of the AAP government over drug abuse, gang violence and security in Punjab. The allegations against Mann and his government form part of the opposition's broader challenge to the state's handling of law and order.

Article Title: 19 killed in Kolkata stampede; CM Suvendu announces jobs, Rs 25 lakh for kin
Article Text:

'Some attempting to politicise this, but it will be to no avail'

'An announcement by the organisers' led to the rush

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday announced a compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a government job for the family of each person killed in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata.The state government will also bear the entire cost of medical treatment for the injured and provide Rs 5 lakh to each of them, Adhikari said, adding that a fact-finding committee would be constituted to investigate the incident."This is a tragic incident. 19 people have lost their lives, 17 of whom died on the spot... 25 people have been injured; 24 of them are out of danger, while one remains in critical condition," the chief minister said. He added that the government was making every possible effort to assist the affected families and that he had personally met relatives of the deceased.Adhikari said the state government would seek the intervention of the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to constitute a fact-finding committee, which would include special task force (STF) and forensic teams. The investigation would examine the circumstances leading to the stampede and identify those responsible for the crowd management arrangements.Kolkata Police's Anti-Rowdy Section (ARS) has collected CCTV footage from the site, which will be examined as part of the investigation."We will check the footage and take appropriate measures against those who failed to manage the crowd. That could be a member of the puja committee, a homeguard, a temporary worker, a policeman, or a private company security guard. Nobody will be spared," Adhikari said.He said the state government was making arrangements for postmortems in accordance with the law and that six of the deceased had been identified so far. Officials were also coordinating with the families of the victims.The chief minister said the families who had met him had expressed faith in the state government. He added that the Prime Minister's Office had sought a report from the chief secretary, which had been submitted, and that the Centre and the state were working together to provide assistance.Adhikari also criticised the previous state government over its handling of past tragedies, accusing some people of attempting to politicise the current incident."Everyone is well aware of the role of the previous government in similar incidents that occurred in the past. Some are attempting to politicize this, but it will be to no avail. I have met with the families of the deceased, and they have explicitly stated that they have full faith in the Chief Minister and the government... The PMO also requested a report from the Chief Secretary, which we have submitted. The Prime Minister has announced relief and compensation. The central and state governments are working together on this..." he said.Referring to other incidents, Adhikari said 13 people had died due to electrocution during the 2025 Puja season amid heavy rain. He also referred to a devastating flood in north Bengal that killed 100 people, questioning the previous chief minister's response to those tragedies.The stampede occurred on Saturday evening, on Maha Saptami, at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata. At least 19 people died and 25 were injured after a crowd surge amid rain, according to officials.A police officer said people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward as it began raining, causing some to fall on the road and triggering the stampede. Adhikari said an announcement made by the organisers of the community Durga Puja had led to a rush among revellers, resulting in what he described as a "painful incident".Officials of the organising club, private security guards and personnel on duty were detained for questioning, he said. The administration also advised several crowded theme-based puja pandals to temporarily close following the tragedy.Union home minister Amit Shah, who had arrived in Kolkata and was scheduled to visit pandals on Sunday, cancelled his programmes following the incident. President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shah and former chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed condolences over the deaths.PM Modi announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 2 lakh for the next of kin of each deceased person and Rs 50,000 for each injured person. The state government has also launched a toll-free helpline to provide information related to the stampede.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced a compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a government job for the family of each person killed in a stampede. The state government will also bear the entire cost of medical treatment for the injured and provide Rs 5 lakh to each of them. A fact-finding committee would be constituted to investigate the incident.

NEW DELHI: A sudden surge of people, heavy rain and alleged confusion over announcements and entry-exit routes are among the factors being investigated after a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening.The incident occurred around 7.15pm on Maha Saptami, when a large crowd waiting on the narrow Radha Madhab Saha Lane to enter the pandal reportedly surged forward as a downpour began. Those already inside were caught in the rush, with people unable to move towards the exit as visitors ahead blocked their way. Several people reportedly fell down a flight of stairs near the exit and were trampled by those behind them.A misleading announcement by the puja committee is also suspected to have added to the confusion, while the blowing of whistles by private security guards may have triggered a rush among visitors, according to CM Adhikari.Kolkata Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy, a senior officer told PTI. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper, leaving visitors confused during peak hours.Locals also questioned the police deployment at the venue, claiming that personnel were largely stationed near the VIP entrance."I have not seen adequate police presence this year. This resulted in the mismanagement," Chorbagan resident Sanghamitra Bhowmik told PTI.Another concern raised by locals was the alleged lack of administrative assistance in taking the injured to hospitals."There must be some lapses, but these should be probed. Whether lapses were on the part of the organisers or they had flouted the rules to erect the pandal will be checked," the police officer told PTI.A forensic team visited the site late on Saturday to collect evidence. Police are questioning the organisers and examining CCTV footage, while also seeking details of the security guards and other personnel deployed to manage the crowd. Officers who were posted at the venue will also be questioned as part of the investigation.Adhikari, who visited the injured at Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, said the incident had raised concerns about safety arrangements at crowded Durga Puja venues. According to hospital sources, 11 injured people were shifted to SSKM Hospital. The deceased included 13 women and a child, a source at the medical college said.The chief minister announced a high-level committee to inspect prominent pandals across West Bengal and review crowd management, exit routes, lighting and structural safety. The panel will be led by Disaster Management Principal Secretary Rajesh Sinha, Fire Services Director General Anuj Sharma and Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Javed Shamim.Adhikari urged organisers to follow official safety recommendations, warning against elaborate themes that compromise visitors' safety. He also called for wider exits, better lighting and the removal of bottlenecks created by temporary rope enclosures. Where complex structures obstruct movement, organisers may be advised to restrict rituals to the inner sanctum and use LED screens outside.The state government has announced Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased victim. A toll-free helpline, 18003455678, has also been set up to help people seeking information about those affected.
Article Summary: A stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening. Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper.

NEW DELHI: MK Stalin on Saturday backed protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, but his latest salvo was directed as much at Congress as at the Election Commission . The DMK chief accused Congress of double standards on the SIR while reminding the party of the opposition alliance's troubles in Bihar, including seat-sharing disputes and Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand Mukti Morcha's decision to contest independently.At a meeting of the DMK Parliamentary Party, Stalin-led DMK adopted four resolutions, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, extending solidarity to student protests against the SIR and seeking electoral reforms. But the resolutions also carried a pointed political message for Congress. The DMK claimed it opposed the SIR before the national opposition campaign gathered momentum, and questioned Rahul Gandhi and Congress's credentials to challenge its record.The party said Stalin first raised his voice against the exercise in July 2025, after reports of large-scale voter deletions emerged from Bihar, where the SIR was first implemented. He also joined the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar, accompanied by DMK deputy general secretary Kanimozhi Karunanidhi.Interestingly, Rahul Gandhi had also claimed that his party was the first to raise the issue. In a press conference held after the Indian Express report, Rahul Gandhi said: "Whether it is due to some confusion or deliberate tampering, the Congress party was the first to raise its voice about the flaws in the SIR process and voter list deletions.When we first raised it, they called it baseless—now the truth is coming out from within the Commission itself. Raja said the latest resolution was intended to lay out a chronological account of the DMK's opposition and questioned whether Congress had the "moral right" to challenge the party on the issue.The DMK also brought the opposition alliance's Bihar experience into the argument, recalling Stalin's remarks after the 2025 Bihar assembly election results were announced on November 15.Stalin had flagged problems within the opposition alliance, including inflexibility over seat-sharing, the JMM's decision to leave the alliance and contest independently, and constituencies where candidates from the Rashtriya Janata Dal, Congress and Left parties fought against one another.The DMK's resolutions also demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an inquiry into his conduct, accusing him of facilitating the disenfranchisement of eligible voters through the SIR. Article Title: Indian woman jailed over son’s fatal stabbing faces possible deportation from UK
Article Text:
Vickrum Digwa's mother Kiran Kaur was jailed for three years in July for assisting an offender

Kirpan argument sparks controversy

Police conduct under investigation

An Indian woman jailed for helping her son after he fatally stabbed an 18-year-old student in Southampton could face deportation to India following her early release from prison, British authorities have indicated.According to new agency PTI, the UK Home Office said it would seek to deport foreign criminals at the earliest opportunity, although it did not refer specifically to Kiran Kaur, 53. Foreign nationals sentenced to at least 12 months in prison are generally considered for deportation, subject to exceptions and legal challenges.Kaur was sentenced to three years in prison in July for assisting an offender by removing the weapon used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill Henry Nowak on December 3, 2025. She is expected to be released early under a government scheme aimed at reducing overcrowding in British prisons.Digwa, 23, was sentenced to life imprisonment in June, with a minimum term of 21 years before he becomes eligible for parole.Both Kaur and her son have been granted permission to challenge their sentences, with their appeals scheduled to be heard by the UK Court of Appeal on November 5.The case drew widespread attention after Digwa sought to invoke a religious self-defence argument involving the kirpan, a ceremonial knife that Sikhs are legally permitted to carry in the UK.During Kaur’s sentencing, Justice William Mousley stressed that the kirpan was a symbol of religious faith and was not intended to be carried for offensive purposes. He said any use of the weapon in self-defence would have to be justified by circumstances involving great seriousness and urgency.The judge also criticised Kaur for removing the weapon rather than challenging her son’s actions and encouraging him to do the right thing.He acknowledged that she had experienced a difficult life in India before marrying and moving to the UK nearly 30 years ago. He said she had acted to protect her son rather than for personal gain and was unlikely to reoffend, while making clear that her actions warranted punishment.British Sikh organisations and parliamentarians subsequently condemned what they described as the misrepresentation of the kirpan, stressing that religious protection did not justify the violence in this case.The killing also triggered scrutiny of police conduct after body-worn camera footage showed officers handcuffing Nowak following Digwa’s allegations that he had been subjected to racism. Those allegations were subsequently rejected in court.The Independent Office for Police Conduct is investigating the officers’ handling of the incident amid allegations of “two-tier” policing, referring to claims that different communities were treated unequally.The case has heightened tensions in Southampton and the wider Hampshire and Isle of Wight area.Kaur’s potential deportation remains subject to the applicable immigration process, while the outcome of the appeals against her sentence and Digwa’s life term is awaited.
Article Summary: Kiran Kaur, 53, was jailed for three years in July for assisting an offender. She removed the weapon used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill Henry Nowak. Home Office said it would seek to deport foreign criminals at the earliest opportunity.

Article Title: 'Verify before she vilifies': India rejects UN rapporteur's claims on youth protests
Article Text:
India rejects UN rapporteur Gina Romero’s claims on youth protests

NEW DELHI: India has rejected allegations by UN special rapporteur Gina Romero that young people in the country face retaliation and stigmatisation for discussing mental health and gender justice, calling the claims based on anonymous and unverified submissions.Speaking at an interactive dialogue with Romero during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee, India’s first secretary Anuj Swarup questioned the evidence cited in her report on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and association.“Yet, the special rapporteur, Ms Gina Romero, asserts that young people in India face retaliation or stigmatisation for discussing mental health or gender justice, though merely citing unnamed submissions in the footnote. This level of arbitrary report writing is precisely the reason that the United Nations and its institutions have lost credibility,” Swarup said.“A sweeping charge against the world's largest youth population resting on anonymous and unverified claims is not evidence. It is hearsay, dressed up as a UN report, and my delegation rejects it outright,” he added.Swarup said India’s Constitution guarantees freedom of assembly, association, speech and expression under Article 19, with these rights protected by an independent judiciary, a free press and the National Human Rights Commission.He also cited young people’s participation in political movements and engagement with senior government leaders as evidence of civic space in the country.“In which repressive state does a satirical youth party question the government, marches on the capital, and then sits across the table with senior national leaders?” he asked, referring to a youth-led political movement mentioned in Romero’s report.“Chair, a mandate holder who relies on anonymous inputs to generalise for 1.4 billion people does a disservice to the very mandate she holds. We urge this special rapporteur to verify before she vilifies and to bring the required rigour and fairness in her reports,” he said.The remarks come amid heightened scrutiny of the government’s handling of youth protests, including demonstrations over alleged irregularities in public examinations and the recent anti-SIR stir.Romero had alleged in posts on X on October 10 that peaceful youth protesters in India faced excessive force and arbitrary detention. She also claimed that more than 2,500 protesters had been sent to remote detention centres without legal support, with some allegedly tortured or sexually assaulted. She further alleged that phones had been seized, protest-related material deleted and internet access restricted.These allegations were made by Romero and were not independently established in the information provided by India’s statement.India, meanwhile, defended its response to student protests over examination irregularities, saying the government had engaged with young people and taken steps to address exam fraud.Swarup said Parliament had amended the Public Examinations Act, doubled punishments for paper leaks, overhauled the examination system and created fast-track courts in every state to prosecute exam fraud.He also pointed to the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue, saying more than five million young people had participated this year and helped shape national priorities through direct engagement with the Prime Minister.
Article Summary: India rejects UN rapporteur Gina Romero’s claims on youth protests in the country. India calls the claims based on anonymous and unverified submissions. Romero had alleged that peaceful youth protesters in India faced excessive force and arbitrary detention. She also claimed that more than 2,500 protesters had been sent to remote detention centres without legal support.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Article Title: Kolkata stampede: 12 detained, including pandal organisers; 19 dead
Article Text:
Several sustained injuries during a stampede-like incident at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal.





KOLKATA: Nineteen people died and 15 others were injured in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata's Chorbagan area on Saturday evening, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said. Kolkata Police said 12 people, including some Puja organisers, have been detained and are being questioned in connection with the incident.The incident took place around 7.40 pm in the Girish Park police station area amid heavy crowds of pandal hoppers and rain.As it started raining, people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward, and some fell on the road, triggering the stampede, a senior officer told PTI.All the injured were rescued and taken to Calcutta Medical College for treatment.An eyewitness told news agency ANI, “Many people lost consciousness; some were being taken on motorcycles. I witnessed this happening all around—when people fainted, they were taken away on bikes. All of this took place, and there was a massive crowd as well...”Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, chief secretary Manoj Agarwal, health minister Saradwat Mukherjee and senior officials reached the hospital to meet the injured.Also Read: Kolkata pandal stampede: Heavy rush amid rain led to deadly incident - top developments Police, fire brigade personnel, disaster management teams and medical teams were rushed to the spot, along with ambulances. The pandal has been closed to visitors.Police have also set up helplines at the Lalbazar Control Room for assistance in connection with the incident. The numbers are 18003455678 and 03322141310.West Bengal governor RN Ravi's office posted on X: "Saddened by the loss of precious lives in the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata. My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief. Praying for the swift recovery of the injured."
Article Summary: The incident took place at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata's Chorbagan area. Police said 12 people, including some Puja organisers, have been detained and are being questioned in connection with the incident. All the injured were rescued and taken to Calcutta Medical College.

Article Title: 5 workers killed, 5 injured in explosion at chemical unit in Gujarat's Bharuch
Article Text:
Explosion at chemical manufacturing unit

(With Agency Inputs)





BHARUCH: At least five workers were killed and five others injured in an explosion at a pharmaceuticals factory in Sayakha GIDC area in Gujarat’s Bharuch, police said.The blast occurred around 10 pm on Friday during a hydrogenation process and triggered a leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas, officials said.Bharuch Sub-Divisional Magistrate Manisha Manani said SynZeal Pharmachem, which was set up in Saykha a year ago, manufactures pharmaceutical intermediates.The explosion, suspected to have occurred during the hydrogenation process, was powerful enough to rip apart the reactor tank, scattering machinery parts across the premises, she said.Superintendent of Police Akshyaraj Makwana said that five people died in the blast, while five others sustained injuries.The deceased were identified as Jaydeep Maheshbhai Patel and Bhavik Dilipkumar Vasava, both from Amod; Vrund Talaviya from Talala in Gir Somnath district; and Uttar Pradesh natives Aniket Harilal Gautam and Arjunkumar Ramsingh Gautam, he said.The injured workers were identified as Pavankumar Ramsingh Gautam, Mausamkumar Ramsevak Yadav, Shivdayal Ramavatar Yadav, Pratik Pravin Prajapati and Priyanshu Bahadurlal.The workers, who hail from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, are undergoing treatment, Makwana said.An official of the Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health (DISH) said the blast during the hydrogenation process triggered a leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas.Officials from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board, DISH and the police reached the site. The cause of the explosion is being investigated.
Article Summary: The blast occurred around 10 pm on Friday during a hydrogenation process and triggered a leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas, officials said. SynZeal Pharmachem, which was set up in Saykha a year ago, manufactures pharmaceutical intermediates.

Article Title: ‘He was under massive debt’: Shraddha Dubey recounts events before Lucknow bizman’s death
Article Text:
Shraddha Dubey has shared a second video asserting her innocence in the tragic case of Shiva Sharma's death

Claims Sharma was under financial stress

Denies torture, recounts events before death

Alleges Sharma’s mother assaulted her driver

Appeals to media, cites mental distress





LUCKNOW: A second video statement by Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma , has surfaced on social media. Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to her arrest.In the video, Dubey denies any role in Sharma’s death, describes it as a suicide and claims that he was under severe financial stress due to debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh. She has also appealed to the media to stop linking her to the case, saying she is under immense mental distress following the incident.Dubey says she had known Sharma for around four months and had been in a relationship with him for approximately two months. According to her, they had not spoken for several days before October 7, when Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor at the main crossing in Lucknow’s Kapurthala area.She claims Sharma was crying when he tried to reach her. Dubey says she called him twice before he called her around 2am and told her he was coming to meet her. He later arrived in his BMW. According to her account, he had consumed alcohol before they met.Dubey says they then went to Pedalers Cafe, where Sharma ordered matcha for her and her driver, along with juice for himself. She claims they later returned home, with Sharma driving her car and her driver driving Sharma’s BMW.Dubey alleges that Sharma had debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh and frequently received calls from creditors when they were together. She claims he had told her that he might take his own life if he failed to repay the money, although she says she did not take his statements seriously at the time.Dubey says she has screenshots of their conversations that she intends to share. She also claims Sharma’s mobile phone has been handed over to the police and that an examination of his call detail records could help establish the nature of the calls he received from creditors and shed light on the circumstances leading to his death.Her claims about Sharma’s debts and state of mind have not been independently verified.Dubey denies that Sharma was subjected to torture or abuse while he was with her. She says Sharma’s friends, whom she identifies as Ashwini Mishra and Harsh, visited them on October 8 and that their interactions were normal.She also says her sister visited her home that day to discuss arrangements for Navratri. According to Dubey, her sister barely knew Sharma and had no connection with the circumstances surrounding his death.Recounting the events of October 9, Dubey says she and Sharma woke up and went to the drawing room to have tea. Sharma then went to the washroom but closed the main entrance door, which she claims was unusual.Dubey says she became suspicious because of his earlier statements about his financial difficulties and asked her sister to check on him. However, she claims Sharma jumped from the balcony before her sister could open the door.Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment near Balu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area on October 9.Dubey claims Sharma’s mother arrived at the hospital after being informed of the incident and assaulted her driver. She says the incident would have been captured on hospital CCTV cameras.She further alleges that Sharma’s family accused her and others of murder without establishing the circumstances surrounding his death. Dubey says CCTV footage, call records and other evidence should be examined to determine what happened.These claims form part of Dubey’s account and have not been independently corroborated.Towards the end of the video, Dubey appeals to the media not to circulate rumours or repeatedly link her to the murder allegations. She says her deteriorating health and mental state prevented her from speaking immediately after the incident.She adds that she is grieving the loss of someone close to her and claims that continued harassment could push her towards suicide.Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of three people in connection with Sharma’s death: Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, and Tanveer Ali, alias Danish, reportedly Dubey’s driver.The investigation into Sharma’s death is continuing. Dubey’s claims about suicide, financial distress and the events leading up to Sharma’s fall remain to be examined by investigators against CCTV footage, call detail records, witness accounts and other available evidence.
Article Summary: Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment near Balu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area on October 9. A second video statement by Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death, has surfaced on social media. Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to her arrest. Dubey claims Sharma had debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh and frequently received calls from creditors when they were together.

Article Title: Out on bail in murder case, man stabbed and shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station near Mumbai
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station by unidentified assailants on Wednesday night





ULHASNAGAR: An accused in a murder case, Haresh Gajwani (54) alias Gajya, was stabbed and shot dead by unidentified assailants outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.The attackers allegedly first assaulted Gajwani with a chopper before firing two rounds at him, one of which hit him, while the other misfired, Vitthalwadi police said. Gajwani was rushed to Central Hospital by locals and police, where doctors declared him “brought dead”. A senior police officer said that they are checking CCTV footage of the area to track down the culprits.Gajwani had reportedly launched campaigns against the illegal sale of gutka, gambling and online gambling in the locality. He was allegedly receiving threats following his efforts to expose these activities, local residents said.Deputy commissioner of police Sachin Gore said Gajwani had a criminal record and a murder case had been registered against him in 2021, in which he was out on bail. Police suspect that the killing may have stemmed from a dispute linked to this case, but are investigating all possible angles, Gore said.Gajwani, who lived with his wife and daughter in Ambernath, had earlier resided in Ulhasnagar’s Camp 4 area, where he was actively involved in social work.Recently, he had posted on X about the alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had tagged senior officials from various police departments as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had also expressed fear for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused should also be held responsible if anything happened to him.His foster sister, Rajni Thakur, told TOI that Gajwani had been working for the welfare of society and had raised his voice against certain people, following which he had allegedly received threats. She demanded a thorough investigation and strict action against those responsible for his murder.Gajwani’s elder son, who suffered from thalassemia, died three years ago after battling the illness for 13 years.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani (54) alias Gajya, was stabbed and shot dead by unidentified assailants outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. Gaj wani had reportedly launched campaigns against the illegal sale of gutka, gambling and online gambling in the locality.

VIJAYAWADA: The Andhra Pradesh government cracked the whip on Kuppam Area Development Authority (KADA) Project Director Vikas Marmat after Bengaluru police registered a criminal case against him and three others following a pub brawl and the alleged abuse and attempted assault of police personnel on October 10.The 2019-batch IAS officer and his three associates — Abhay Uday Singh, a real estate businessman; Nitish, the owner of a competitive exam coaching centre in Bihar; and Roshan, a bouncer — were booked by Cubbon Park police for allegedly abusing and attempting to assault a team of police personnel, including police inspector Arun Salunke, at an upscale bar and restaurant on Residency Road in Bengaluru around 1.30am on October 10.The IAS officer was named as the primary accused, while the others were listed as co-accused. Police said Marmat and the others apologised for their conduct the following morning.The incident took place when a Central Crime Branch team visited Cavore around 1.30am as part of a drive to check underage revelry at liquor outlets. The pressure was particularly acute because Marmat serves as the project director of the urban development authority in Kuppam, the constituency represented by Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu After the chief minister directed the chief secretary to conduct a detailed inquiry and submit a report on the incident on October 13, the state government swiftly initiated disciplinary action against Marmat. He was transferred and directed to report to the General Administration Department (GAD) for further posting on Wednesday.The state government also directed the Chittoor collector to make suitable arrangements for an in-charge project director at KADA.
Article Summary: The Andhra Pradesh government cracked the whip on Kuppam Area Development Authority (KADA) Project Director Vikas Marmat. Article Title: ‘Will save many mothers from trauma’: Saurabh Rajput’s mother on Muskan, Sahil’s death sentence
Article Text:

'Sentence will save mothers from trauma'





MEERUT: A woman and her lover were sentenced to death on Wednesday for murdering her merchant navy officer husband, dismembering his body and sealing the remains in a cement-filled blue plastic drum at their Meerut home in March 2025. The verdict in the sensational ‘blue drum’ murder case that hit headlines across the country came 15 days after their conviction. It followed 126 hearings and examination of 22 prosecution witnesses. While awarding capital punishment, the judge invoked the Mahabharata, observing that “punishment is also dharma”.District and sessions judge Arvind Kumar Mishra sentenced Muskan Rastogi, 27, and her lover Sahil Shukla, 25, for murdering Muskan’s husband, Saurabh Rajput, 29. The prosecution sought the death penalty, arguing that the crime fell within the ‘rarest of rare’ category. The convicts appeared through video conferencing, while Rajput’s mother, Renu Devi, attended the proceedings in person.Prosecution lawyer KK Chaubey said the judge referred to the Mahabharata while explaining that punishing offenders in proportion to the gravity of their crimes was also a “righteous duty”.The court also imposed fines of Rs 50,000 each for murder under section 103(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Rs 20,000 each for causing disappearance of evidence under section 238.Rajput’s family lawyer Vijay Bahadur said, “We had cited three cases of a similar nature in which the courts had given death sentences.” The slain merchant navy man’s mother broke down outside the courtroom.“My son cannot come back, but I had prayed every day for the last 18 months that they should be given the death sentence. I am thankful to Mata Rani for hearing my prayers. I am sure this kind of sentence will serve as a deterrent and will save many mothers from the trauma I have experienced,” she said.The murder took place in March 2025 at the couple’s Meerut home. Investigators said Muskan sedated Rajput before she and Sahil killed him with a sharp weapon. They subsequently dismembered his body and concealed the remains in a blue plastic drum using cement and sand. The case would eventually find notoreity across India and come to be known as the “blue drum murder”.During the trial, the prosecution presented forensic and circumstantial evidence, along with testimony concerning the purchase of the drum, cement, sand and cutting tools. The court convicted both on Sept 30.
Article Summary: Muskan Rastogi, 27, and her lover Sahil Shukla, 25, sentenced to death on Wednesday. Sentenced for murdering her merchant navy officer husband, dismembering his body and sealing the remains in a cement-filled blue plastic drum at their Meerut home.

Article Title: 'It was suicide, not murder': Model Shraddha Dubey breaks silence in Shiva Sharma death case
Article Text:
Image Credit: X





LUCKNOW: A day after being named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma , model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey surfaced in a video posted on social media, denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials and said she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.The 1-minute-15-second video emerged even as Lucknow Police intensified efforts to trace the accused. On Tuesday, police announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and Tanveer Ali alias Danish in connection with the case.In the video, Dubey alleged that rumours were being spread about her and objected to what she described as attempts to link her to politicians and bureaucrats based on social media associations.“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she said, appealing to the media not to draw conclusions without evidence.Dubey also denied that she was absconding and claimed she intended to cooperate with investigators.“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said.Dubey asserted that Sharma’s death was not a murder. “The truth is that Shiva Sharma did not die due to murder but by suicide,” she said, adding that she was currently not in a condition to explain the circumstances in detail because of her health.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.Following the incident, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. The family has alleged that Dubey pushed Sharma from the building, a claim that investigators are examining.All those named in the FIR remain untraceable. In a recent development, an SUV allegedly linked to Dubey was found abandoned near the India-Nepal border in Bahraich district.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey claims Shiva Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder. She urges the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials. The 1-minute-15-second video emerged even as Lucknow Police intensified efforts to trace the accused.

Article Title: Skidding bikes spark road safety debate over Kolkata flyover rainbow paint
Article Text:
Image Credit: X





KOLKATA: A viral video showing three motorcycles skidding on the rainbow-painted Chingrighata flyover after a drizzle has raised questions concerning motorists’ safety. Has the festive road beautification drive compromised with safety parameters for the sake of aesthetics?While the exact circumstances of the incidents in the viral footage remain to be independently established, highway engineering principles suggest that inappropriate surface coatings can reduce tyre grip, particularly when wet. CM Suvendu Adhikari told reporters, “Bikes can skid for various reasons. I will not make any statement without knowing what has actually happened.”Senior state minister Agnimitra Paul said KMDA, police and civic engineers had been sent to the spot at Chingrighata flyover to look into the matter.“The painting has been done to keep up with the mood of the festive season and that it is not a permanent feature.We will take steps as per recommendations of the experts,” Paul told TOI on Wednesday. A senior engineer associated with the West Bengal Traffic and Transport Planning Directorate questioned whether the authorities used road-grade, skid-resistant material or ordinary decorative paint. “The paint does not appear to be a thermoplastic road-marking material. It looks more like oil-based or emulsion paint. Road surfaces require technically-approved materials,” the engineer said.The concern has a scientific basis. Tyre grip depends on the friction generated between the rubber and the road’s textured surface.A smooth coating can cover the asphalt’s microscopic irregularities, reducing friction. When rainwater accumulates, braking and cornering become particularly hazardous for two-wheelers, said a road engineer with the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI).Specially formulated coloured surfacing systems incorporating anti-skid aggregates can provide adequate friction even in wet conditions, the engineer said. An important distinction, engineers say, is that thermoplastic paint is not automatically suitable for coating an entire carriageway. Decorative applications covering large areas require appropriate coloured surfacing systems and separate friction assessments. The controversy also revives questions about mastic asphalt surfaces. The Kolkata Police and Bidhannagar Police stated that no one has complained yet. “We have informed all agencies involved with the painting that this can be dangerous,” said a senior Kolkata Police source.
Article Summary: A viral video showing three motorcycles skidding on the rainbow-painted Chingrighata flyover after a drizzle has raised questions concerning motorists’ safety. Has the festive road beautification drive compromised with safety parameters for the sake of aesthetics? Highway engineering principles suggest that inappropriate surface coatings can reduce tyre grip.

Article Title: Heavy traffic expected on Pune-Mumbai Expressway, old highway; police urge use of public transport
Article Text:
Traffic police in Pune have asked citizens to prefer public transport during the Navratri festival period.





PUNE: Traffic police have requested people to use public transport as much as possible with heavy vehicular rush being expected on both Pune-Mumbai expressway and the old highway this weekend through Tuesday.The district administration has already ordered the diversion of heavy and large vehicles from the old highway to alternative routes from Thursday to prevent congestion during Shri Ekvira Devi Navratri festival. Highway police have also increased patrolling on the expressway to ensure that heavy vehicles do not occupy the first two lanes.The order issued by the collector on Tuesday under Section 115 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, prohibits entry of heavy and large vehicles round the clock on the stretch between Karla Phata and the foothill temple of Shri Ekvira Devi until Oct 20.It further says that from Oct 15 to 19, heavy and large vehicles will not be allowed on the old Mumbai-Pune highway between Kusgaon Budruk toll plaza in Lonavla and Vadgaon Phata in Vadgaon Maval, from 6 am to 10 pm. Vehicle operators have been advised to use Mumbai-Pune expressway via Urse toll plaza as an alternative route.With Dasara on Tuesday being a holiday, people who are planning to take off from work on Monday, or take the work-from-home option, may have an extended weekend holiday.Vijay Pandey, a businessman living in Borivali, Mumbai, said, “I am travelling to Pune to visit my friends. I usually drive. But this time, I and my partner are planning to book Vande Bharat to travel. We don’t want to get stuck on the highway,” he said.Shivaji Pawar, superintendent of police (SP), Highway Traffic Police, Pune range, said heavy vehicles travelling to and from Chakan and Talegaon to Mumbai will be diverted to the expressway, due to which the vehicular movement on the Mumbai-Lonavala stretch of the expressway is expected to increase.“We have already had a discussion with Pune Rural Police regarding traffic management. We will engage 50 of our total strength of 60 on ground during the weekend. Moreover, rural police station personnel will also be in full force managing the traffic. We are hoping that more people will travel via railways and use public transport during these days as pilgrims are expected to come in large numbers, especially during the weekend and towards the last days of Navaratra till Tuesday. We urge people to restrain from travelling if avoidable during the heavy rush days,” said Pawar, adding that they have been imposing fines on heavy vehicles that do not follow lane discipline.As per the collector’s order, the heavy vehicles travelling towards Pune on the old Mumbai-Pune highway will be diverted via Kusgaon Budruk toll plaza in Lonavala onto the Expressway and towards Pune city through Urse toll plaza. Similarly, heavy vehicles travelling towards Mumbai will be diverted from Talegaon Phata in Vadgaon through Urse Ghat and onto Mumbai-Pune expressway. Height barriers have been installed at Karla Phata to prevent heavy and large vehicles from proceeding towards Shri Ekvira Devi temple during the restricted period.
Article Summary: Heavy vehicular rush expected on Pune-Mumbai expressway and old highway this weekend through Tuesday. Highway police have increased patrolling on the expressway to ensure that heavy vehicles do not occupy the first two lanes. District administration has already ordered the diversion of heavy and large vehicles from the old highway to alternative routes from Thursday.

Article Title: Lover hits woman on head, burns her body with room heater in Maharashtra over marriage demand
Article Text:
A court remanded him in police custody till October 17, said an official. (AI Image)

(With Agency Inputs)





NAGPUR: A 38-year-old married woman was allegedly murdered by her lover, who hit her on the head with a heavy object and inflicted burns on her body using a room heater before fleeing, police said on Wednesday.According to news agency PTI, the MIDC Police arrested the accused, Javed Sheikh Shahid Manyar (33), from Jalgaon in north Maharashtra on Tuesday,A court remanded him in police custody till October 17, an official said.The woman, whose name has not been disclosed, lived with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13.Javed, a resident of Raver tehsil in Jalgaon district, worked as an air-conditioner technician in Nagpur, the official said."The woman and Javed had known each other for around 15 years and were in a relationship. She had been pressuring him to marry her. Since Javed was already married, the issue led to frequent disputes," the official said.Javed visited the woman's house on Sunday morning when her husband had gone to his native village for work and her daughters were at their uncle's house."An argument broke out between the two over the marriage issue in the evening.Javed allegedly hit the woman on the head with a heavy object. He then allegedly inflicted burns on her body using a room heater," the official said.The accused fled to Jalgaon by train that night. The incident came to light on Monday morning when the woman's daughters returned home.The family initially suspected that she had died of an electric shock.However, a preliminary medical report indicated that the woman had suffered a head injury. Javed was arrested on Tuesday and brought to Nagpur.
Article Summary: Javed Sheikh Shahid Manyar (33), from Jalgaon in north Maharashtra, remanded in police custody. The woman, whose name has not been disclosed, lived with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13. She and Javed had known each other for around 15 years and were in a relationship.

Article Title: Mumbai Fire: Two women die in Nalasopara tower blaze; Navratri event power connection suspected to have triggered short circuit
Article Text:
fire broke out in the Imperial Heritage building located in Nalasopara East, resulting in the tragic loss of two women from smoke inhalation





NALASOPARA: Two women died and six people were injured after a major fire broke out in the 14-storey Imperial Heritage residential building in Achole, Nalasopara East, on Tuesday night. Police suspect that a short circuit, possibly linked to an electricity connection taken for a Navratri celebration organised within the building premises, might have triggered the fire.The deceased were identified as Falguni Shah (58) and Ashwini Parkar (55), both residents of the 12th floor. They died of suffocation caused by smoke inhalation, said Achole police station senior inspector SujitKumar Pawar. Three of the six people injured in the incident required hospital treatment; the other three sustained minor injuries.More than 25 residents trapped on the upper floors were rescued by the fire brigade with the help of cranes and by breaking open doors that had become difficult to open due to the heat. The blaze raged for nearly six hours before being completely extinguished around 6 am on Wednesday.The building has three wings and 154 flats. The fire broke out around 11.30 pm, reportedly after sparks emerged from electrical wiring on the 13th floor.It soon intensified and spread to other floors, forcing residents to rush downstairs. However, those living between the ninth and 14th floors were trapped as smoke and flames spread through the building.Gauri Khamkar, an injured resident of the 11th floor, recounted her ordeal. “I was sleeping at home when my neighbours informed me about the fire. I was alone inside the flat for nearly an hour, shouting for help. The smoke made it difficult to breathe. Finally, I called people I knew, who came and broke open the door to rescue me,” she said.Resident Sunil Mahadik said the lifts stopped working during the fire, while several doors became difficult to open as they swelled due to the heat.Flats on the ninth and 12th floors suffered extensive damage, while several other homes were partially damaged. The fire originated in flat 903. Police said the flat was completely gutted after the fire brigade ran out of water while attempting to douse the flames.The building’s construction was completed in 2022, but it had not yet been formally handed over by the builder. Although fire safety equipment was installed, it was not operational, said resident Lalit Dubey.Police are investigating the cause of the fire, including the possibility of a short circuit linked to the temporary electricity connection used for the Navratri celebration.
Article Summary: Two women died and six people were injured after a major fire broke out in the 14-storey Imperial Heritage residential building in Achole, Nalasopara East, on Tuesday night. Police suspect that a short circuit, possibly linked to an electricity connection taken for a Navratri celebration organised within the building premises, might have triggered the fire. The deceased were identified as Falguni Shah (58) and Ashwini Parkar (55), both residents of the 12th floor.

Article Title: Punjab anti-drug activist’s killer held in op shrouded in secrecy
Article Text: MANSA: Medical store owner Ashwani Kumar, who gunned down anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa on Tuesday, has been arrested, police said on Wednesday.The administration bulldozed ‘illegally constructed' sections of his house and shop but it did nothing to ease the anger raging in the region. Protesters have called a Punjab bandh on Friday — with all opposition parties and farmer groups backing it.The details of Kumar’s arrest seem shrouded in secrecy. All day, news channels reported that he was caught in Rajasthan’s Salasar (over 300 km from Mansa), but when TOI asked Bathinda DIG Harjit Singh, he said Kumar was arrested “somewhere in Punjab”. Reports about his arrest from Rajasthan weren’t true, he said, but didn’t give out any further information. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday condemned the murder and said: “I have directed the DGP to ensure a thorough investigation so that the truth comes out and everyone involved in this crime is identified. The main accused has been arrested within 24 hours. If the probe reveals the involvement of any other individual or organisation in a conspiracy behind this murder, they will not be spared.”Jhota’s supporters and Mansa locals are seething. Hundreds of them blocked Mansa-Sirsa road even as political functionaries made a beeline for the town to lend support to the protest.There was heavy police deployment on Wednesday and opposition parties said many of their functionaries were stopped from reaching Mansa.Jhota’s ex-Serviceman father, Bhim Singh, warned that he would drive to nakas on his motorbike and personally bring activists to town if police tried to stop them. If anything untoward happens, police would be responsible for it, he said. Jhota’s family continued to decline to perform the last rites till justice was delivered. If Mansa observes a bandh on Thursday, it would mean three days of shutdown.Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh, former PCC chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, former Congress chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, former SAD MP Simranjit Singh Mann, SAD working president Balwinder Singh Bhundar and Akali Dal Waris Punjab De MP Sarabjit Singh Khalsa were among a large number of political activists who addressed the protesters and pledged support to the fight for justice.Members of Nihang Singh and Sikh organisations, farmer groups, youth and student organisations stood shoulder to shoulder with members of Left-leaning organisations. Waris Punjab De alleged that its senior functionaries were put under house arrest or detained at different places to stop them from reaching Mansa.The protesters resolved to make Punjab bandh call successful and reiterated their demand to remove Punjab DGP from his post.Even as protests continued, the district administration demolished parts of the home and shop of accused Ashwani Kumar. Bathinda DIG Harjit Singh said as per a district administration report, some illegal encroachments were noticed and removed. It was the protesters who completely razed the shop and a better part of the home, said police. Mansa deputy commissioner Navjot Kaur was not available for comment.The bulldozing was questioned by several residents, including Jhota’s supporters. The alleged encroachments or illegal constructions had stood for decades, so why was it now that the administration suddenly discovered them, they asked, arguing that it was akin to punishing Kumar’s family members for his crime.
Article Summary: Ashwani Kumar, who gunned down anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa on Tuesday, has been arrested, police said on Wednesday. Protesters have called a Punjab bandh on Friday — with all opposition parties and farmer groups backing it.

Article Title: ‘He beat and strangled her’: Woman found dead at in-laws’ home in Gurgaon
Article Text:
It said that Bhavna had been staying at her parental home for around five months because of the alleged harassment.





GURGAON: A 25-year-old woman, who had allegedly been harassed over dowry, was found dead in Farrukhnagar on Tuesday.Her family has accused her husband and in-laws of assaulting and strangling her, even as the in-laws told police she had consumed poison.A case was registered against the victim’s husband, Gautam Sharma, his father, Bijender Sharma, who retired from Indian Air Force, and his younger brother, Ashu Sharma.According to the complaint filed by the deceased’s father, Anil Sharma , a resident of Khera village in Hapur district of UP, his daughter Bhavna married Gautam on Dec 16, 2023. The couple also had a son. The family alleged that Gautam and his family harassed her over dowry and demanded Rs 25 lakh. The complainant stated that the family had paid Rs 2.5 lakh in cash a few months earlier.It said that Bhavna had been staying at her parental home for around five months because of the alleged harassment. Her brother, Ajay Sharma, said Gautam took her back around Raksha Bandhan, promising to live separately from his parents and take responsibility for her. Ajay alleged that the abuse resumed within a few days of her return.Ajay said the family spoke to Bhavna on Tuesday afternoon. According to him, she told her father that Gautam was beating her and that he was strangling her. Ajay said his father subsequently spoke to Gautam, who denied that anything had happened and claimed that Bhavna wanted to return to her parental home.Bhavna’s elder sister, Rashmi Sharma, said her sister had called their father at around 3.30pm, complaining of physical assault and asking to be taken home. Rashmi said she tried to contact Bhavna but could not get through. She alleged that Gautam later answered a call, after which his mother took the phone and reassured the family that there was no problem. At 4.47pm, the family learnt that Bhavna had been taken to hospital and was declared dead, Rashmi said.Ajay said the family was later informed that she had died after consuming poison, a claim they dispute. The family alleged that Bhavna’s body bore marks around the neck, injuries on the back and signs of a struggle, and suspect that she was assaulted. Police said these allegations were yet to be established through the investigation and postmortem findings.Rashmi said that when the family reached the matrimonial home, Gautam and his parents were not present. She also claimed that neighbours told them Gautam had been married previously. Ajay similarly alleged that the family learnt after Bhavna’s death that Gautam had been married before. Police said they are yet to verify these allegations.The family has also accused the police of inaction and delay. Ajay alleged that police personnel arrived late at night despite her death in the afternoon, and that the family had to wait for several hours for further action. Gaurav, a cousin of Bhavna, alleged that the family had initially struggled to obtain police assistance at the hospital. He said they had requested that a zero FIR be registered if jurisdiction was an issue, so that the case could subsequently be transferred to the appropriate police station. According to him, the family was made to wait before Farrukhnagar police arrived.The family further alleged that they were misled into signing documents during the inquest proceedings which stated that Bhavna had died after consuming poison. They questioned why their signatures were sought on a version of events they disputed and demanded clarity on the medical findings.A protest broke out outside the local postmortem facility, where the family raised slogans against police. The protesters then visited the local police headquarters.Station house officer (SHO) of Farrukhnagar police station rejected the allegations and said a fair probe had been initiated. “We initially had information that the victim died after consuming poison and thus documents were prepared accordingly. There is no reason for the police to force the family and get their signature on false papers. We have booked the accused for dowry death and will nab them soon. The reason behind her death will be ascertained through the autopsy report,” the SHO said.The case was registered at Farrukhnagar police station under sections 80 (dowry death), 85 (husband or relative subjecting a woman to cruelty) and 3(5) (act done by multiple persons) of BNS.
Article Summary: A case was registered against the victim’s husband, Gautam Sharma, his father, Bijender Sharma, and his younger brother, Ashu Sharma. The complainant stated that the family had paid Rs 2.5 lakh in cash a few months earlier. Bhavna had been staying at her parental home for around five months.

Article Title: Gujarat man burns 2-year-old son alive, buries body to destroy evidence
Article Text:
A man allegedly set his son Navghan on fire using petrol





PALANPUR: A man allegedly burned his two-and-a-half-year-old son alive after dousing him with petrol at Suigam in Vav-Tharad district, before burying the body at a cremation ground in an attempt to destroy evidence, police said.The killing came to light after the accused’s uncle lodged a complaint with Suigam police. The accused, Ashok Raval, allegedly considered raising his son, Navghan, a burden, as his wife had been living separately for some time.According to the complaint filed by Babu Raval, a resident of Ravalvas in Suigam, Ashok had married a woman from Himmatnagar. She had been living separately, leaving him to care for their young son alone. With no one to look after the child, Ashok found the responsibility of raising him increasingly difficult.On Oct 13, between 1pm and 2pm, Ashok allegedly poured petrol on Navghan and set him on fire. He later took the toddler to a hospital, where the child died.To conceal the circumstances of the death, Ashok, along with family members, buried the child’s body at the community burial ground rather than allowing the cause of death to come to light.Babu later learnt about the matter and approached Suigam police, filing a complaint against his nephew.Police conducted an excavation at the burial ground in the presence of officials, including the mamlatdar, and exhumed the child’s body for further investigation.Suigam police registered a case against Ashok for murder and causing disappearance of evidence.
Article Summary: A man allegedly burned his two-and-a-half-year-old son alive after dousing him with petrol at Suigam in Vav-Tharad district. The accused, Ashok Raval, allegedly considered raising his son, Navghan, a burden, as his wife had been living separately.

Article Title: 2 women dead as fire breaks out in 14-storey Imperial Heritage building in Nalasopara, over 25 rescued
Article Text:
A devastating fire erupted on the 11th floor of a residential building in Nalasopara East





NALASOPARA: Two women died after a major fire broke out at the 14-storey Imperial Heritage residential building in Achole, Nalasopara East, on Tuesday night.Fire brigade personnel and police rescued more than 25 residents trapped inside the building. The blaze was brought under control after nearly six hours. A short circuit is suspected to have triggered the fire, officials said.The fire broke out at around 11.30 pm on the ninth floor of the building's B wing. It soon intensified and spread to the upper floors, reaching the 14th floor and triggering panic among residents.Many rushed downstairs to save their lives, while several others were trapped inside as thick smoke and flames spread through the building.The deceased have been identified as Ashwini Parkar (55) and Falguni Shah (58), who lived on the 12th floor. Shah was reportedly unwell and bedridden, making it difficult for her to escape. Both women died of suffocation, police said.Fire engines from the Vasai-Virar Municipal Corporation's fire brigade rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident. Firefighters and police personnel launched a rescue operation to evacuate residents trapped on the upper floors."The lifts were not working due to the fire, and some doors had swollen due to the heat and become difficult to open. We had to break open doors to rescue people," said Achole police station senior inspector Sujit Kumar Pawar.The building has 154 flats. Arrangements have been made to accommodate around 110 residents in the hall of a nearby hotel, officials said.Police said the presence of a large amount of wooden furniture and decorative items inside flats may have contributed to the rapid spread of the fire.Mayor Ajiv Patil, MLA Sneha Dubey Pandit and municipal commissioner Prithviraj B P reached the spot to take stock of the situation. Additional fire engines from the Mira-Bhayandar Municipal Corporation were also called in to assist with firefighting operations.The blaze was brought under control at around 5.30 am on Wednesday, nearly six hours after it broke out.
Article Summary: Fire broke out at around 11.30 pm on the ninth floor of the building's B wing. It soon intensified and spread to the upper floors, reaching the 14th floor and triggering panic among residents. The deceased have been identified as Ashwini Parkar (55) and Falguni Shah (58)
